title: Label Noise in Segmentation Networks: Mitigation Must Deal with Bias
mechanism: Evidence paper: segmentation nets are robust to unbiased label errors (random warp, crop) but sensitive to biased errors (constant shift), so mitigation must target bias.
adaptation: Not an arm. Frames which part of our crack IoU loss is recoverable: per-source width and any per-source constant offset (biased) vs within-source jitter (unbiased). Motivates the zero-GPU per-source offset / width diagnostics and a benchmark report of biased-error sensitivity.
min_experiment: Zero-GPU: per-source mean signed offset of label skeleton to ridge (x, y) and label width on train labels; plus per-source predicted width on CV OOF. Decision rule: proceed with style arms only if a source deviates by > 0.3 px in offset or > 0.15 px in width between prediction and label.
evidence: R: BraTS-type tumour masks; constant 5 px shift cost about 10% Dice for supervised, MT and AE models; random warps barely hurt.
